questions.prompt: Which art element is mainly used to show the outline of a drawn object?
options: Line
Tempo
Dialogue
Tuning
questions.correctAnswer: Line
questions.explanation: A line can mark the edge, direction, and shape of an object in a drawing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic visual elements used in drawing.

questions.prompt: Which word describes how rough, smooth, soft, or hard a surface looks or feels?
options: Texture
Melody
Formation
Pitch
questions.correctAnswer: Texture
questions.explanation: Texture describes the surface quality of an artwork or material.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize visual qualities used to describe artworks.

questions.prompt: Which colour is made by mixing red and yellow paint?
options: Orange
Green
Purple
Blue
questions.correctAnswer: Orange
questions.explanation: Red and yellow are primary colours that mix to make orange.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall simple secondary colour mixtures.

questions.prompt: What is a repeated design, shape, colour, or movement called?
options: Pattern
Script
Audience
Tonic
questions.correctAnswer: Pattern
questions.explanation: A pattern is created when elements are repeated in an organized way.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify repeated elements in creative work.

questions.prompt: Which tool is most suitable for measuring and drawing a straight border?
options: Ruler
Whistle
Drumstick
Costume
questions.correctAnswer: Ruler
questions.explanation: A ruler helps measure length and draw straight lines accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Name tools used for neat picture preparation.

questions.prompt: Which homemade instrument can be made by putting dry seeds in a sealed container?
options: Shaker
Recorder
Violin bow
Paint brush
questions.correctAnswer: Shaker
questions.explanation: A shaker produces sound when dry objects inside it move and strike the container.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple percussion instruments made from safe local materials.

questions.prompt: How do string instruments mainly produce sound?
options: Their strings vibrate
Their pages turn
Their colours mix
Their actors speak
questions.correctAnswer: Their strings vibrate
questions.explanation: A string instrument sounds when a stretched string vibrates after being plucked, bowed, or struck.
questions.learningOutcome: State how string instruments produce sound.

questions.prompt: In French rhythm names, which term is commonly used for two short sounds in one beat?
options: Ta-te
Taa-aa
Taa-aa-aa-aa
Rest
questions.correctAnswer: Ta-te
questions.explanation: Ta-te represents two shorter sounds that fit into one beat.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize basic French rhythm names used in class patterns.

questions.prompt: Which sol-fa syllable comes immediately after mi in the scale d r m f s l t d'?
options: Fa
Re
La
Ti
questions.correctAnswer: Fa
questions.explanation: In the sol-fa ladder, fa comes after mi.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the order of sol-fa syllables within one octave.

questions.prompt: What do we call an organized tune made from different pitches?
options: Melody
Texture
Prop
Boundary
questions.correctAnswer: Melody
questions.explanation: A melody is a tune formed by arranging pitches in a musical line.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic music vocabulary used in melody work.

questions.prompt: In a written play, what tells actors what to do or how to move?
options: Stage directions
Colour wheel
Weft thread
Landing area
questions.correctAnswer: Stage directions
questions.explanation: Stage directions guide actors' movements, actions, and sometimes feelings during a scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify parts of a simple drama script.

questions.prompt: What is the arrangement of dancers in a performance space called?
options: Formation
Volume
Montage
Tension
questions.correctAnswer: Formation
questions.explanation: A formation shows where dancers stand or move in relation to each other.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize basic dance organization terms.

questions.prompt: Which item is most important for safe landing during high jump practice?
options: Soft landing area
Paint palette
Recorder case
Script page
questions.correctAnswer: Soft landing area
questions.explanation: A soft landing area reduces injury risk when a learner comes down after a jump.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic safety equipment for high jump practice.

questions.prompt: Which volleyball skill is mainly used to receive a low ball with the forearms?
options: Dig pass
High jump
Stencil print
Mime
questions.correctAnswer: Dig pass
questions.explanation: A dig pass uses joined forearms to control a low or fast ball.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic volleyball skills practised in upper primary.

questions.prompt: A simple gymnastics sequence should have which basic structure?
options: Beginning, middle, and ending
Only shouting and running
Only paint and glue
Audience, ticket, and shop
questions.correctAnswer: Beginning, middle, and ending
questions.explanation: A clear sequence starts, develops through linked movements, and finishes with control.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the basic structure of a movement sequence.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner plan a drawing before adding colour?
options: To organize shapes, space, and details clearly
To hide all mistakes under wet paint
To avoid thinking about the subject
To make every picture look the same
questions.correctAnswer: To organize shapes, space, and details clearly
questions.explanation: Planning helps the artist place objects well before final colours and details are added.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of planning in picture making.

questions.prompt: What does value mean when discussing colour in a painting?
options: How light or dark a colour is
How loudly a song is sung
How many actors are on stage
How fast a player runs
questions.correctAnswer: How light or dark a colour is
questions.explanation: Value describes the lightness or darkness of a colour or tone.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain colour value in visual artwork.

questions.prompt: Which group contains warm colours often used to show heat, energy, or brightness?
options: Red, orange, and yellow
Blue, green, and violet
Black, grey, and white
Brown, navy, and silver
questions.correctAnswer: Red, orange, and yellow
questions.explanation: Red, orange, and yellow are called warm colours because they can suggest warmth and energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify colours according to simple colour families.

questions.prompt: Why is balance important in a picture composition?
options: It helps parts of the artwork feel well arranged
It makes all objects disappear
It replaces the need for colour
It turns a drawing into a song
questions.correctAnswer: It helps parts of the artwork feel well arranged
questions.explanation: Balance distributes visual weight so one part of the artwork does not feel awkwardly heavy.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how composition affects the appearance of artwork.

questions.prompt: Which description best explains a collage?
options: An artwork made by sticking different materials onto a surface
A song performed without rhythm
A jump over a volleyball net
A script with no characters
questions.correctAnswer: An artwork made by sticking different materials onto a surface
questions.explanation: Collage uses materials such as paper, fabric, leaves, and photographs arranged on a base.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe collage as a picture-making technique.

questions.prompt: How is a montage different from a single drawing?
options: It combines several images or parts to communicate one idea
It uses only one straight line
It can only be performed by dancers
It has no message or theme
questions.correctAnswer: It combines several images or parts to communicate one idea
questions.explanation: A montage joins different images so they work together around a chosen theme.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how montage communicates an idea.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to make art with clean reusable materials?
options: It reduces waste while providing safe creative materials
It makes the classroom dirty on purpose
It prevents learners from designing anything
It removes all need for planning
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces waste while providing safe creative materials
questions.explanation: Using clean reusable materials supports creativity and responsible care for the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain environmental responsibility in selecting art materials.

questions.prompt: Why should raised parts of a printing block be clear and firm?
options: They carry the paint or ink that makes the print
They stop all patterns from appearing
They make the paper tear easily
They are used only for singing
questions.correctAnswer: They carry the paint or ink that makes the print
questions.explanation: In simple block printing, raised areas receive colour and transfer the design to paper or fabric.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how simple relief printing works.

questions.prompt: In weaving, what does the weft thread usually do?
options: It passes over and under the warp threads
It tunes a string instrument
It gives stage directions
It marks the volleyball court
questions.correctAnswer: It passes over and under the warp threads
questions.explanation: The weft is woven across the fixed warp threads to build the fabric or mat.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of warp and weft in simple weaving.

questions.prompt: Which qualities make a decorated craft item more attractive and useful?
options: Neat finishing, suitable pattern, and strong construction
Loose parts, sharp edges, and no purpose
Hidden holes and weak joining
Random dirt and wet glue
questions.correctAnswer: Neat finishing, suitable pattern, and strong construction
questions.explanation: A good craft item should be well made, safe to handle, and decorated in a purposeful way.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain qualities of a well-finished craft item.

questions.prompt: What is an instrumental ensemble?
options: A group of people playing instruments together
One learner drawing alone
A silent audience line
A pile of unused props
questions.correctAnswer: A group of people playing instruments together
questions.explanation: An ensemble performs when different players coordinate their instruments as a group.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe instrumental ensemble performance.

questions.prompt: Why should instruments be tuned before an ensemble performance?
options: So their sounds blend well together
So dancers can paint faster
So the audience cannot hear them
So the instruments become heavier
questions.correctAnswer: So their sounds blend well together
questions.explanation: Tuning helps instruments match pitch and sound pleasant when played together.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of tuning in group music performance.

questions.prompt: What role does a drum often play in a song or dance performance?
options: Keeping a steady rhythm
Writing the script
Mixing secondary colours
Measuring the high jump bar
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping a steady rhythm
questions.explanation: A drum can guide performers by keeping the beat and supporting movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of percussion in performance.

questions.prompt: Which method can help create an interesting rhythm pattern?
options: Repeating and varying note values
Using no beat at all
Changing every sound randomly
Ignoring the tempo of the activity
questions.correctAnswer: Repeating and varying note values
questions.explanation: Rhythm becomes clearer and more interesting when repetition is balanced with variation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain simple techniques for composing rhythmic patterns.

questions.prompt: What does stepwise movement mean in a simple sol-fa melody?
options: Moving to the next nearby sol-fa pitch
Jumping across many pitches every time
Singing without any pitch
Only clapping the rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: Moving to the next nearby sol-fa pitch
questions.explanation: Stepwise movement uses neighbouring pitches, such as d to r or m to f.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe stepwise melodic movement.

questions.prompt: Why does a melody need a suitable ending?
options: It helps the tune feel complete
It makes the tune impossible to sing
It removes all rhythm
It changes the song into a painting
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the tune feel complete
questions.explanation: A clear ending gives the listener a sense that the musical idea has finished.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of an ending in melody composition.

questions.prompt: What are dynamics in music?
options: How loud or soft sounds are performed
How rough a mat feels
How high a player jumps
How many pictures are pasted
questions.correctAnswer: How loud or soft sounds are performed
questions.explanation: Dynamics show the volume level in singing or playing instruments.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain basic performance terms used in music.

questions.prompt: Which tempo is usually safest for starting a warm-up movement activity?
options: Moderate and controlled
Very fast from the first second
Random and confusing
Stopped with no movement
questions.correctAnswer: Moderate and controlled
questions.explanation: A warm-up should begin with controlled movement so the body prepares safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe tempo choices for movement preparation.

questions.prompt: Which elements often work together in a Kenyan folk dance performance?
options: Song, rhythm, movement, formation, and costume
Only silent standing in one place
Only a written mathematics table
Only a painted frame
questions.correctAnswer: Song, rhythm, movement, formation, and costume
questions.explanation: Folk dances commonly combine music, movement, dress, and group organization to express meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe elements used in folk dance performance.

questions.prompt: What do high, middle, and low levels refer to in dance?
options: The height of body movements in space
The price of costumes
The size of paint brushes
The number of drum skins
questions.correctAnswer: The height of body movements in space
questions.explanation: Dance levels describe whether movement is performed high, near the middle, or close to the floor.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain levels used in dance movement.

questions.prompt: How can an actor show that a character is worried without saying it directly?
options: Use facial expression, posture, and voice carefully
Hide behind the audience throughout
Paint the stage floor only
Stop all movement and leave
questions.correctAnswer: Use facial expression, posture, and voice carefully
questions.explanation: Drama uses expression, body movement, and voice to communicate a character's feelings.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how actors communicate character feelings.

questions.prompt: Why are props useful in a drama performance?
options: They help show action, setting, or character
They replace all actors
They stop the audience from watching
They make dialogue unnecessary every time
questions.correctAnswer: They help show action, setting, or character
questions.explanation: A prop is an object used on stage to support the story and make action clearer.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of props in drama.

questions.prompt: Why should a group rehearse before presenting a creative arts performance?
options: To improve timing, confidence, and teamwork
To avoid learning the performance
To make everyone forget their roles
To keep mistakes hidden forever
questions.correctAnswer: To improve timing, confidence, and teamwork
questions.explanation: Rehearsal helps performers practise roles, correct errors, and coordinate as a group.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of rehearsal before performance.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows good audience etiquette during a class performance?
options: Listening quietly and applauding respectfully
Shouting over the performers
Walking across the stage without reason
Laughing to embarrass classmates
questions.correctAnswer: Listening quietly and applauding respectfully
questions.explanation: A respectful audience allows performers to be heard and supports them appropriately.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain respectful behaviour when observing creative works.

questions.prompt: What information is useful on a label for displayed artwork?
options: Title, artist, materials, and theme
Only the viewer's shoe size
Only the classroom noise level
Only the lunch menu
questions.correctAnswer: Title, artist, materials, and theme
questions.explanation: A label helps viewers understand who made the work, what it is called, and what materials were used.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe useful information for displaying creative works.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a drawn pot to look round. Which shading choice is best?
options: Make one side darker and keep the light side lighter
Colour the whole pot one flat tone
Erase the outline after colouring
Write the word round beside it only
questions.correctAnswer: Make one side darker and keep the light side lighter
questions.explanation: Light and dark shading can make a form look more rounded and solid.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply shading to show form in a drawing.

questions.prompt: Which plan would make a clear school poster about tree planting?
options: Use a bold tree image, short message, and readable lettering
Fill the page with tiny unrelated words
Use only hidden colours on a dark background
Leave the poster blank until presentation day
questions.correctAnswer: Use a bold tree image, short message, and readable lettering
questions.explanation: A poster communicates best when the main image and message are easy to see and understand.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply composition principles to communicate a theme.

questions.prompt: How can a learner make a tint of blue paint?
options: Add a little white to blue
Add black soil to blue
Mix blue with a whistle
Leave blue paint uncovered overnight
questions.correctAnswer: Add a little white to blue
questions.explanation: A tint is made by adding white to a colour to make it lighter.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply colour mixing to create tints.

questions.prompt: Which safe method can create visual texture on paper using a leaf?
options: Place paper over the leaf and rub gently with a crayon
Burn the leaf under the paper
Cut the leaf with a rusty blade
Pour dirty water over the drawing
questions.correctAnswer: Place paper over the leaf and rub gently with a crayon
questions.explanation: Texture rubbing transfers the surface pattern safely when done with clean materials and gentle pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe techniques for creating texture effects.

questions.prompt: Which material choice is safest for a recycled collage in class?
options: Clean dry cartons, paper, and fabric pieces
Broken glass and rusty metal strips
Wet food waste and sharp tins
Dirty medical waste containers
questions.correctAnswer: Clean dry cartons, paper, and fabric pieces
questions.explanation: Clean dry materials are safer to handle and can still support creative reuse.
questions.learningOutcome: Select safe reusable materials for artwork.

questions.prompt: A woven bookmark has loose threads at the edges. What should the learner do?
options: Tuck or tie the ends neatly to secure the weave
Pull out all the warp threads
Wet the whole bookmark with glue only
Ignore the edges because finishing does not matter
questions.correctAnswer: Tuck or tie the ends neatly to secure the weave
questions.explanation: Securing loose ends improves strength, neatness, and durability.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply finishing techniques to simple woven items.

questions.prompt: A string instrument sounds too low because the string is very slack. What should be done carefully?
options: Tighten and tune the string gradually
Cut the string immediately
Paint the string thicker
Cover the sound hole with paper
questions.correctAnswer: Tighten and tune the string gradually
questions.explanation: Increasing string tension can raise pitch, but it should be done gradually to avoid damage.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic tuning ideas to string instruments.

questions.prompt: During an instrumental ensemble, the drum is so loud that the melody cannot be heard. What should the drummer do?
options: Play more softly to balance with the group
Play even louder than everyone
Stop following the beat completely
Face away and ignore the leader
questions.correctAnswer: Play more softly to balance with the group
questions.explanation: Good ensemble playing requires listening and adjusting volume so all parts work together.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply balance and listening skills in ensemble performance.

questions.prompt: Which rhythm would best support a group doing a steady warm-up march?
options: A regular moderate beat
A very uneven beat with long pauses
A sudden shout after every step
No beat at all
questions.correctAnswer: A regular moderate beat
questions.explanation: A regular moderate beat helps learners coordinate safe warm-up movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply rhythm to guide movement activities.

questions.prompt: If taa is 1 beat, ta-te is 1 beat, and taa-aa is 2 beats, which pattern fills four beats?
options: Taa, ta-te, taa-aa
Taa, taa, ta-te, taa-aa-aa-aa
Ta-te, taa-aa, taa-aa
Taa-aa, taa-aa, taa-aa
questions.correctAnswer: Taa, ta-te, taa-aa
questions.explanation: The beats add up as 1 plus 1 plus 2, making four beats.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply beat values to create a four-beat rhythm pattern.

questions.prompt: Which role plan would help a class instrumental ensemble perform clearly?
options: Assign melody, rhythm, and support parts, then practise together
Let every learner play a different tempo
Choose roles only after the performance ends
Hide the main instrument behind the class
questions.correctAnswer: Assign melody, rhythm, and support parts, then practise together
questions.explanation: Clear roles and joint practice help the ensemble stay organized and balanced.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply role allocation in group music performance.

questions.prompt: Which sol-fa pattern is easiest for a beginner melody using mostly stepwise movement?
options: d r m r d
d l f t r
m d' s r t
d s d' f l
questions.correctAnswer: d r m r d
questions.explanation: The pattern moves mostly between neighbouring pitches and returns to d.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply sol-fa knowledge to choose a singable melody pattern.

questions.prompt: A short melody feels unfinished. Which change would most likely make it sound complete?
options: End on d after a clear repeated idea
Stop suddenly on a random high note
Remove all rhythm from the melody
Sing every pitch at once
questions.correctAnswer: End on d after a clear repeated idea
questions.explanation: Ending on the home pitch d often gives a simple sol-fa melody a finished feeling.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply melodic ending techniques in simple composition.

questions.prompt: Which action best describes a safe underarm volleyball serve?
options: Stand behind the line, hold the ball, and swing the other arm under control
Throw the ball at a classmate's face
Serve while standing inside the opponent's court
Kick the ball over the net
questions.correctAnswer: Stand behind the line, hold the ball, and swing the other arm under control
questions.explanation: An underarm serve uses controlled arm movement from behind the service line.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply correct basic technique for underarm serving.

questions.prompt: How should a learner position the arms for a volleyball dig pass?
options: Join forearms, keep elbows straight, and bend knees slightly
Wave one hand high above the head
Cross arms behind the back
Hold the ball and run with it
questions.correctAnswer: Join forearms, keep elbows straight, and bend knees slightly
questions.explanation: A stable forearm platform and bent knees help control a low ball safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply body positioning for the dig pass.

questions.prompt: Before high jump practice, which safety check should the group make?
options: The landing area is soft, clear, and supervised
The bar is hidden from learners
The runway is wet and slippery
The jump starts before instructions
questions.correctAnswer: The landing area is soft, clear, and supervised
questions.explanation: High jump practice needs a safe landing area, clear space, and teacher guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety checks before high jump activities.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is suitable for a simple three-phase gymnastics routine?
options: Start balance, controlled roll, finish shape
Sprint blindly, collide, and sit down
Paint a mat, sing loudly, and leave
Throw a ball, hide, and clap once
questions.correctAnswer: Start balance, controlled roll, finish shape
questions.explanation: A gymnastics sequence should link controlled movements with a clear start and finish.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply sequencing to create controlled gymnastics movement.

questions.prompt: Which mat safety practice is best before practising rolls?
options: Check that the mat is dry, flat, and placed in clear space
Use a torn mat with exposed sharp parts
Place the mat on stones
Start rolling while others cross the mat
questions.correctAnswer: Check that the mat is dry, flat, and placed in clear space
questions.explanation: A safe mat and clear space reduce slipping, tripping, and collisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety rules for gymnastics practice.

questions.prompt: What should learners do if there is no teacher or lifeguard near a swimming area?
options: Stay out of the water and wait for supervision
Enter quickly before anyone sees
Practise alone in deep water
Push each other into the water
questions.correctAnswer: Stay out of the water and wait for supervision
questions.explanation: Swimming activities require supervision and clear safety rules.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety rules for water activities.

questions.prompt: A dance group keeps bumping into each other while entering the stage. What should they improve?
options: Spacing, pathways, and entry formation
Paint mixing only
The price of costumes only
The title of the song only
questions.correctAnswer: Spacing, pathways, and entry formation
questions.explanation: Clear spacing and planned pathways help dancers move safely and neatly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply space awareness in group dance performance.

questions.prompt: Which costume choice is best for a school folk dance?
options: Respectful clothing that fits the theme and allows safe movement
Very tight clothing that stops movement
Sharp metal pieces that scratch others
Random clothing chosen to mock a community
questions.correctAnswer: Respectful clothing that fits the theme and allows safe movement
questions.explanation: Costumes should support the dance meaning, respect culture, and keep performers safe.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable costume ideas for folk dance performance.

questions.prompt: Which drama plan best fits a short improvised scene about a lost school bag?
options: Assign roles, show the problem, search honestly, and resolve it
Let all actors shout unrelated words
Hide the bag and never explain the story
Remove the setting and all characters
questions.correctAnswer: Assign roles, show the problem, search honestly, and resolve it
questions.explanation: A good improvised scene needs roles, a clear problem, believable actions, and a resolution.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple story structure in improvisation.

questions.prompt: In mime, which action would best show that a bucket is heavy?
options: Bend the knees, strain the arms, and move slowly
Smile and wave empty hands quickly
Jump lightly with no effort
Turn away and speak loudly
questions.correctAnswer: Bend the knees, strain the arms, and move slowly
questions.explanation: Mime communicates weight through controlled body action and facial expression without words.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply body movement to communicate meaning in mime.

questions.prompt: Why should learners warm up before dance or gymnastics?
options: To prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
To make the floor slippery
To skip practice instructions
To make breathing harder immediately
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
questions.explanation: Warm-up activities gradually prepare the body for more active movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply warm-up principles before movement activities.

questions.prompt: Which activity is suitable for cooling down after vigorous movement?
options: Slow walking and gentle stretching
Sudden racing without rest
Holding breath while jumping
Pushing classmates for space
questions.correctAnswer: Slow walking and gentle stretching
questions.explanation: Cooling down helps the body return to a resting state safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cool-down practices after movement activities.

questions.prompt: Why might a group record its own performance during rehearsal with permission?
options: To observe timing, movement, and areas to improve
To embarrass performers online
To avoid practising again
To replace the teacher's guidance
questions.correctAnswer: To observe timing, movement, and areas to improve
questions.explanation: Recording with permission can help learners review their work and plan improvements responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use feedback tools responsibly to improve performance.

questions.prompt: Which display plan is safest for a classroom exhibition?
options: Hang artworks neatly with labels and leave clear walking space
Pile all work on the floor near the door
Block the doorway with display tables
Let visitors touch wet glue and paint
questions.correctAnswer: Hang artworks neatly with labels and leave clear walking space
questions.explanation: Safe display allows viewers to move easily and understand the works without damaging them.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe organization when displaying artworks.

questions.prompt: Which peer comment gives useful and respectful feedback on a drawing?
options: Your shading shows form well; make the background neater
This is bad and I will not say why
Only my friend's work is good
You should stop drawing forever
questions.correctAnswer: Your shading shows form well; make the background neater
questions.explanation: Helpful feedback names a strength and gives a clear suggestion for improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful feedback when reviewing creative work.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to sell handmade greeting cards at a school fair. Which pricing idea is sensible?
options: Consider material cost, time, neatness, and a fair small profit
Choose any price without checking costs
Make the cards dirty to seem old
Charge less than the cost of materials every time
questions.correctAnswer: Consider material cost, time, neatness, and a fair small profit
questions.explanation: Craft pricing should consider costs, effort, quality, and a fair return.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple entrepreneurship ideas to creative products.

questions.prompt: Which action shows integrity when using another artist's idea for inspiration?
options: Create an original version and acknowledge the source of inspiration
Copy the whole artwork and write your name on it
Hide the source and pretend it is fully yours
Sell copied work as original
questions.correctAnswer: Create an original version and acknowledge the source of inspiration
questions.explanation: Responsible artists learn from others while making their own work and giving credit where needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrity when creating original artwork.

questions.prompt: Which poster plan would communicate a handwashing message most clearly?
options: Large handwashing image, short slogan, strong contrast, and readable letters
Many tiny pictures with no main message
A blank page with a long speech beside it
Dark letters on a dark background only
questions.correctAnswer: Large handwashing image, short slogan, strong contrast, and readable letters
questions.explanation: A clear public message needs a strong main image, brief words, and readable contrast.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze design choices that make a poster effective.

questions.prompt: A landscape drawing looks flat although it has many objects. Which change would best suggest depth?
options: Overlap some objects and make distant objects smaller
Make every object the same size in one row
Erase the horizon and all shadows
Put all colours in one corner
questions.correctAnswer: Overlap some objects and make distant objects smaller
questions.explanation: Overlapping, size change, and placement can help show near and far space.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ways to show depth in a drawing.

questions.prompt: A border pattern looks confusing because motifs are crowded and uneven. What is the best improvement?
options: Repeat the motif with clear spacing and consistent direction
Add more motifs in every empty space
Change the motif after every centimetre
Cover the whole border with glue
questions.correctAnswer: Repeat the motif with clear spacing and consistent direction
questions.explanation: Spacing and consistency make a repeated pattern easier to see and more attractive.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze pattern arrangement for visual clarity.

questions.prompt: A collage begins falling apart during display. Which issue most likely caused the problem?
options: Unsuitable adhesive or poorly prepared materials
Too many respectful labels
A clear theme and careful cutting
Enough drying time before display
questions.correctAnswer: Unsuitable adhesive or poorly prepared materials
questions.explanation: Collage materials need suitable glue, clean surfaces, and enough drying time to hold firmly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze causes of weak collage construction.

questions.prompt: A woven mat has wavy sides and gaps between rows. Which problem should the learner check first?
options: Uneven tension and spacing while weaving
The title of the performance
The loudness of a drum
The colour of the classroom wall
questions.correctAnswer: Uneven tension and spacing while weaving
questions.explanation: Consistent tension and spacing help woven items keep straight edges and a firm surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze craftsmanship issues in woven products.

questions.prompt: An instrumental ensemble sounds unpleasant because some instruments are not matching pitch. What should the group analyze first?
options: Tuning and listening between players
The colour of the instruments
The number of spectators outside
The size of the classroom windows
questions.correctAnswer: Tuning and listening between players
questions.explanation: Pitch problems in an ensemble are often improved by tuning and careful listening.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze musical balance and tuning in ensemble work.

questions.prompt: A rhythm composition sounds like unrelated beats. Which choice would best create unity?
options: Use a short repeated rhythm idea with small variations
Change every beat without repeating anything
Ignore the time pattern completely
Let each performer choose a different beat secretly
questions.correctAnswer: Use a short repeated rhythm idea with small variations
questions.explanation: A repeated rhythmic idea gives unity, while small variations keep the pattern interesting.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze structure in rhythm composition.

questions.prompt: A class melody is difficult to sing because it jumps widely after almost every note. What is the best revision?
options: Use more stepwise movement and a few narrow leaps
Add even wider leaps throughout
Remove all sol-fa syllables
Sing it in four unrelated tempos
questions.correctAnswer: Use more stepwise movement and a few narrow leaps
questions.explanation: Stepwise movement and narrow leaps usually make a melody easier for learners to sing accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze melodic movement for singability.

questions.prompt: A dance performance has good steps but messy changes between formations. What should the group improve?
options: Transitions, counts, and movement pathways
Only the spelling of the dance title
Only the number of chairs in class
The colour of the drum skin
questions.correctAnswer: Transitions, counts, and movement pathways
questions.explanation: Smooth transitions depend on clear counts, planned pathways, and rehearsed spacing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze movement organization in group dance.

questions.prompt: A drama scene is confusing because the audience cannot tell what problem the characters are solving. What should be added?
options: A clear conflict, sequence of actions, and resolution
More unrelated props on stage
Actors speaking over each other throughout
A hidden ending that no one can see
questions.correctAnswer: A clear conflict, sequence of actions, and resolution
questions.explanation: Drama becomes easier to follow when the problem, actions, and outcome are clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze story structure in a drama performance.

questions.prompt: The audience struggles to hear a play because actors face away while speaking softly. Which improvement fits the problem?
options: Face the audience more often and project the voice clearly
Add more paint to the stage floor
Make the scene shorter but still unclear
Turn all actors completely away
questions.correctAnswer: Face the audience more often and project the voice clearly
questions.explanation: Voice projection and body orientation help the audience hear and understand dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze performance techniques that improve communication.

questions.prompt: A volleyball team keeps missing low balls during dig practice. Which technical issue is most likely?
options: Players are not bending knees or forming a stable forearm platform
Players are reading too many artwork labels
The ball has too much colour contrast
The court has too many song lyrics
questions.correctAnswer: Players are not bending knees or forming a stable forearm platform
questions.explanation: Low balls are easier to control when players bend knees and use joined forearms.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze body positioning in volleyball dig passing.

questions.prompt: During high jump, a learner lands near the edge of the mat. What should be corrected before the next jump?
options: Approach direction, take-off point, and landing area position
The title of the art display
The number of dialogue lines
The colour of the whistle only
questions.correctAnswer: Approach direction, take-off point, and landing area position
questions.explanation: Safe high jump requires an approach and take-off that lead the learner to the centre of the landing area.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safety and technique in high jump practice.

questions.prompt: A gymnastics routine has several movements but no controlled finish. Why is this a weakness?
options: A controlled finish shows balance, completion, and body control
A finish is never needed in gymnastics
It proves the routine has too much safety
It makes the mat too soft
questions.correctAnswer: A controlled finish shows balance, completion, and body control
questions.explanation: The finish helps the audience and performer see that the sequence has ended with control.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze qualities of a complete gymnastics sequence.

questions.prompt: Which approach shows respect when adapting a Kenyan folk dance for school performance?
options: Learn the meaning, use respectful movements, and avoid mocking the community
Change sacred or serious parts into jokes
Use random costumes to ridicule people
Copy movements without asking what they mean
questions.correctAnswer: Learn the meaning, use respectful movements, and avoid mocking the community
questions.explanation: Cultural dances should be handled with understanding, respect, and guidance from knowledgeable people.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze cultural respect in folk dance presentation.

questions.prompt: An exhibition corner is crowded, and visitors cannot view the artwork safely. Which solution is best?
options: Reduce crowding, create a clear route, and space the displays
Add more tables into the doorway
Hang work where no one can see it
Let visitors push through in any direction
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce crowding, create a clear route, and space the displays
questions.explanation: Good exhibition planning protects people and artworks while making viewing easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safety and visibility in artwork display.

questions.prompt: Which review method is fairest when judging classmates' creative work?
options: Use agreed criteria such as skill, effort, message, and finishing
Give high marks only to close friends
Judge by the cost of materials only
Ignore the work and guess randomly
questions.correctAnswer: Use agreed criteria such as skill, effort, message, and finishing
questions.explanation: Agreed criteria make feedback fairer and focused on the work itself.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze fair criteria for reviewing creative work.

questions.prompt: A group project is delayed because everyone wants the same role. Which leadership choice is best?
options: Discuss strengths, share roles fairly, and rotate where possible
Cancel the project immediately
Let the loudest learner take every role
Exclude learners who disagree
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss strengths, share roles fairly, and rotate where possible
questions.explanation: Fair role sharing uses learners' strengths and keeps the group working together.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze teamwork decisions in group creative projects.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows environmental care during a craft lesson?
options: Use safe reusable materials and dispose of scraps properly
Cut fresh plants wastefully without permission
Throw glue containers into drainage
Leave sharp offcuts on the floor
questions.correctAnswer: Use safe reusable materials and dispose of scraps properly
questions.explanation: Responsible making includes safe material choice, waste control, and care for the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze responsible material use in creative work.

questions.prompt: A homemade percussion instrument has sharp nails and loose glass pieces. What is the best judgement?
options: It is unsafe and should be remade with smooth sealed materials
It is safe because it may sound loud
It should be used only by the youngest learners
It needs more glass to improve rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: It is unsafe and should be remade with smooth sealed materials
questions.explanation: Creative instruments should produce sound without exposing learners to cuts or loose dangerous parts.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safety in making percussion instruments.

questions.prompt: Which plan best creates an integrated performance about a market day?
options: Combine short drama, song, rhythm, movement, props, rehearsal, and clear roles
Ask one learner to speak alone with no preparation
Use random actions that do not show a market
Skip rehearsal and hide all props
questions.correctAnswer: Combine short drama, song, rhythm, movement, props, rehearsal, and clear roles
questions.explanation: An integrated performance works best when different creative elements support one theme and are rehearsed.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a plan that combines drama, music, movement, and props.

questions.prompt: Which design plan would make a strong poster about saving water at school?
options: Use a balanced layout, clear water symbol, short slogan, and strong contrast
Fill the page with unrelated decorations only
Use tiny pale words that cannot be read
Copy a classmate's poster exactly
questions.correctAnswer: Use a balanced layout, clear water symbol, short slogan, and strong contrast
questions.explanation: A strong poster uses composition, symbols, and readable text to communicate a clear message.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a purposeful visual communication plan.

questions.prompt: Which rhythm plan best supports a gymnastics sequence with a calm start, strong middle, and quiet finish?
options: Soft steady beats, stronger beats for main movements, then slower quiet beats
One loud random crash from start to finish
No beat until the routine is over
Fast shouting that ignores all movements
questions.correctAnswer: Soft steady beats, stronger beats for main movements, then slower quiet beats
questions.explanation: Matching rhythm to movement phases can support the mood and structure of a gymnastics sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Create rhythm patterns that match movement structure.

questions.prompt: Which sol-fa plan would help create a singable Grade 6 melody?
options: Use repetition, stepwise movement, a few narrow leaps, and an ending on d
Use only wide random leaps and no ending
Choose pitches without rhythm or order
Sing every sol-fa syllable at the same time
questions.correctAnswer: Use repetition, stepwise movement, a few narrow leaps, and an ending on d
questions.explanation: A singable melody is easier to learn when it has structure, manageable movement, and a clear ending.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple melody using sol-fa principles.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares a respectful Kenyan folk dance presentation?
options: Research the dance, understand its meaning, assign roles, rehearse safely, and acknowledge the source
Copy movements without learning their meaning
Make fun of costumes and gestures
Let performers invent claims about a community
questions.correctAnswer: Research the dance, understand its meaning, assign roles, rehearse safely, and acknowledge the source
questions.explanation: Respectful performance combines cultural understanding, teamwork, safety, and honest acknowledgement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a respectful plan for presenting a folk dance.

questions.prompt: Which plan would best turn handmade bead bracelets into a small school enterprise?
options: Survey buyers, make neat samples, price fairly, package safely, and keep records
Make bracelets with weak knots and guess prices
Hide the products and avoid feedback
Spend all money before counting costs
questions.correctAnswer: Survey buyers, make neat samples, price fairly, package safely, and keep records
questions.explanation: A creative enterprise needs quality products, fair pricing, customer feedback, and simple records.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple enterprise plan for a creative product.

questions.prompt: A learner prefers making props instead of dancing. Which inclusive performance plan is best?
options: Assign prop-making, rhythm, narration, and movement roles according to strengths
Force every learner to dance the same part
Leave the prop maker out of the group
Cancel the performance because roles differ
questions.correctAnswer: Assign prop-making, rhythm, narration, and movement roles according to strengths
questions.explanation: Inclusive planning lets learners contribute through different useful roles in the same performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an inclusive role plan for group performance.

questions.prompt: Which set of criteria would best assess a Grade 6 creative project fairly?
options: Creativity, skill, message, teamwork, safety, and finishing
Only the artist's handwriting
Only the cost of materials
Only whether the viewer knows the maker
questions.correctAnswer: Creativity, skill, message, teamwork, safety, and finishing
questions.explanation: Fair assessment looks at the quality of the work and process, not unrelated personal details.
questions.learningOutcome: Create fair criteria for reviewing creative projects.

questions.prompt: Which digital feedback plan is most responsible after recording a class rehearsal?
options: Get permission, review strengths and improvements, store or delete the video responsibly
Post the video publicly to embarrass mistakes
Record secretly and refuse to discuss feedback
Edit the video to mock performers
questions.correctAnswer: Get permission, review strengths and improvements, store or delete the video responsibly
questions.explanation: Digital tools should support learning while respecting privacy and dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a responsible plan for using digital feedback in Creative Arts.

questions.prompt: Which plan best creates an original artwork about a Kenyan community celebration?
options: Observe respectfully, choose meaningful symbols, plan composition, and use original design
Copy a whole picture from the internet
Use random symbols without understanding them
Draw unrelated sports equipment only
questions.correctAnswer: Observe respectfully, choose meaningful symbols, plan composition, and use original design
questions.explanation: Original community-inspired artwork should be respectful, planned, and based on meaningful observation.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an original idea inspired by community creative practices.
